A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViSurf study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, reward-control ablations, training-dynamics analyses, and RLVR run-variability results, including Tables 1–8.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical evaluations and appendix results and adds qualitative task outputs in Figure 7.

M1.justification: The augmented rollout objective, Algorithm 1, and three reward-control mechanisms are retained. The single-sampling/single-update explanation and task-dependent reasoning qualification clarify the existing procedure and ablation choices rather than establish a method change.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluated tasks remain the same, including segmentation, GUI grounding, industrial anomalies, skin lesions, mathematics, and VQA. v3 Figure 7 illustrates existing task coverage; Appendix E largely relocates v1 Section 4.1.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods, including SFT, RLVR, SFT→RLVR, and the LISA, GSVA, SAM4MLLM, SegZero, and VisionReasoner comparisons in Table 7. Newly cited hybrid-training works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Matched settings retain the same splits, sample counts, metrics, learning rate of 1e-6, and batch sizes of 32 for SFT and 16 for RLVR/ViSurf. Added statements about sampling, single-update execution, and excluding VQA fine-tuning data disclose details without establishing revised experiments.

E4.justification: New Section 4.6 and Figure 7 add qualitative examples across existing tasks. Figure 3(c) retains the non-object failure case but removes its displayed RLVR reasoning excerpt. Reward-control ablations, prompt comparisons, training-dynamics analyses, and appendix randomness analysis remain.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix A becomes v3 Appendix B, retaining the approximately one-in-ten RLVR success discussion and Table 8's 90%/10% run labels. No additional run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–8 are retained. Figure 7 adds qualitative outputs. v3 also removes the assertion that RLVR is weakest on both Qwen2VL tasks; Table 3 already shows SFT below RLVR on RealIAD, 56.7 versus 57.1.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), normalized advantages, policy approximation, and gradient decomposition remain mathematically equivalent. Equation (10) moves into Section 3.5. The single-update explanation supplies implementation context for the existing unclipped derivation rather than a new formal result.

C1.justification: The introduction adds an explicit novelty distinction between ViSurf's unified objective and prior approaches described as summing SFT and RLVR losses. The central claims about single-stage integration, reward control, performance, and reduced forgetting otherwise remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 changes the suggested cause of OmniACT degradation from possible test-data contamination to likely overfitting during pretraining, without a new supporting test. Section 3.2 shifts its SFT interpretation from incoherent reasoning toward learning object absence. Existing limitations and future-work discussion are relocated intact.

D1.justification: v3 specifies single-update execution, VQA evaluation after fine-tuning without VQA data, and construction and empty-list targets for the existing 200 non-object examples. Conversely, v1's explicit repository link is removed and replaced by a promise of future code, data, and model availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds Ma et al. (2025) and Zhang et al. (2025), positioning ViSurf against their approaches to combining supervision and RL. Molmo/Pixmo and Llama 3.2 citations are removed. These are limited changes within the retained research framing.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, conclusion, and several method/results passages undergo extensive rewriting. Gradient interpretation moves between subsections; discussion and detailed dataset settings move into appendices. A qualitative-results subsection and an Impact Statements section are added.

P2.justification: The document-wide template change alters the title block, headers, typography, captions, tables, and appendix layout. Figure 3 is redrawn and Figure 7 added. Former Tables 9–10 become narrower, redesigned Prompt 1–2 boxes, while most existing plots and numerical displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added implementation, VQA-control, and negative-example details improve reproducibility documentation, while removing the unsupported RLVR ranking makes the discussion more faithful to Table 3. Figure 7 provides useful illustrations. These are modest gains, tempered by loss of the explicit repository link and reasoning excerpt; the revised OmniACT causal explanation also remains unsupported by a dedicated test.
